'''Egbert Willem Meijer''' (born 1955) is a Dutch organic chemist, known for his work in the fields of [[supramolecular chemistry]], [[materials chemistry]] and [[polymer chemistry]]. Meijer, who is distinguished professor of Molecular Sciences at [[Eindhoven University of Technology]] (TU/e) and Academy Professor of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]], is considered one of the founders of the field of [[Supramolecular polymers|supramolecular polymer chemistry]]. Meijer is a prolific author, sought-after academic lecturer and recipient of multiple awards in the fields of organic and polymer chemistry. In 2025, he was elected to the [[American Philosophical Society]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.amphilsoc.org/news/aps-elects-new-members-2025 | title=APS Elects New Members for 2025 }}</ref>

== Education ==
After attending secondary school in [[Appingedam]] where he graduated in 1972, Meijer received his education in [[Organic chemistry|Organic Chemistry]] at the [[University of Groningen]]. He obtained his [[Master of Science|MSc]] degree in 1978, and subsequently his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree under supervision of Professor Hans Wijnberg in 1982. Meijer graduated summa cum laude with his thesis<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Meijer|first=Egbert Willem|date=1982|title=Chemiluminescence in action. Syntheses, properties, and applications of 1,2-dioxetanes|url=http://www.rug.nl/research/portal/publications/chemiluminescence-in-action-syntheses-properties-and-applications-of-12dioxetanes(32f20b18-59fc-4a35-a9c6-8506edf49bf7).html|type=Thesis fully internal (DIV) |language=English}}</ref> on 'Chemiluminescence in action: syntheses, properties, and applications of 1,2-dioxetanes'.

== Career ==
Meijer started his career in 1982 at the [[Philips Natuurkundig Laboratorium|Philips Research Laboratories]] in Eindhoven as a research scientist in Molecular Materials. In 1989 he moved to [[DSM (company)|DSM]] Research in Geleen to become head of the department for New Materials. In 1991 Meijer was installed as full professor of Organic Chemistry at the department for Chemistry & Chemical Engineering of Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) and in 1999 at the department for Biomedical Engineering at the same university. Since 2004 Bert Meijer is a distinguished university professor of Molecular Sciences at TU/e, where he founded the Institute for Complex Molecular Systems<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.tue.nl/onderzoek/instituten-groepen-scholen/toponderzoeksgroepen/institute-for-complex-molecular-systems/|title=Institute for Complex Molecular Systems|website=www.tue.nl|language=nl-NL|access-date=2017-07-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170702170101/https://www.tue.nl/onderzoek/instituten-groepen-scholen/toponderzoeksgroepen/institute-for-complex-molecular-systems/|archive-date=2017-07-02|url-status=dead}}</ref> and served as its Scientific Director from 2008 until 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tue.nl/en/news/news-overview/06-02-2018-jan-van-hest-named-the-new-scientific-director-of-icms/|title=Jan van Hest named the new scientific director of ICMS|website=www.tue.nl|language=English|access-date=2020-03-01|archive-date=2019-06-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190621154133/https://www.tue.nl/en/news/news-overview/06-02-2018-jan-van-hest-named-the-new-scientific-director-of-icms/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Meijer is adjunct professor of Macromolecular Chemistry at [[Radboud University Nijmegen]] since 1994 and distinguished visiting professor at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] since 2008. In 2014 Bert Meijer was inducted as Academy Professor<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tue.nl/en/university/departments/chemical-engineering-and-chemistry/news/24-04-2014-bert-meijer-appointed-as-academy-professor-by-knaw/|title=Bert Meijer appointed as Academy Professor by KNAW|website=www.tue.nl|language=en-US|access-date=2017-07-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728215046/https://www.tue.nl/en/university/departments/chemical-engineering-and-chemistry/news/24-04-2014-bert-meijer-appointed-as-academy-professor-by-knaw/|archive-date=2017-07-28|url-status=dead}}</ref> of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences.

== Contributions to research ==
Meijer's research focuses on [[Supramolecular chemistry|supramolecular systems]] with special properties and functions. It's founded on the principles of [[Chemical synthesis|synthetic]] and [[organic chemistry]] to find solutions to challenges in materials science and life sciences. Meijer is recognized as a pioneer in the field of supramolecular materials, being one of the first chemists to explore and develop functional [[supramolecular polymers]] as a new class of materials. Via advanced [[Molecular engineering|molecular design]] and synthesis he has realized systems in which [[Monomer|monomeric units]] [[Self-assembly|self-assemble]] into long supramolecular polymeric chains, resulting in materials displaying unique dynamic properties that were thought to be exclusively reserved for [[macromolecule]]s. His new class of supramolecular structures thus led to an adjusted definition of [[Hermann Staudinger|Staudinger]]’s description of what [[polymer]]s are.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brunsveld|first1=L.|last2=Folmer|first2=B. J. B.|last3=Meijer|first3=E. W.|last4=Sijbesma|first4=R. P.|date=2001-12-01|title=Supramolecular Polymers|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=101|issue=12|pages=4071–4098|doi=10.1021/cr990125q|pmid=11740927|issn=0009-2665}}</ref>

Meijer's career took off with breakthrough results in [[dendrimer]] chemistry<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mariani|first1=Giacomo|last2=Schweins|first2=Ralf|last3=Gröhn|first3=Franziska|date=2016-11-22|title=Electrostatic Self-Assembly of Dendrimer Macroions and Multivalent Dye Counterions: The Role of Solution Ionic Strength|journal=Macromolecules|volume=49|issue=22|pages=8661–8671|doi=10.1021/acs.macromol.6b00565|bibcode=2016MaMol..49.8661M|issn=0024-9297}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hest|first1=J. C. M. van|last2=Delnoye|first2=D. a. P.|last3=Baars|first3=M. W. P. L.|last4=Genderen|first4=M. H. P. van|last5=Meijer|first5=E. W.|s2cid=20067098|date=1995-06-16|title=Polystyrene-Dendrimer Amphiphilic Block Copolymers with a Generation-Dependent Aggregation|journal=Science|language=en|volume=268|issue=5217|pages=1592–1595|doi=10.1126/science.268.5217.1592|issn=0036-8075|pmid=17754610|bibcode=1995Sci...268.1592V|hdl=2066/17428|url=https://research.tue.nl/nl/publications/653628fb-364d-4b52-9875-c851078732f9 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> including a dendritic box and super-[[amphiphile]]s (being the first examples of [[polymersome]]s). He synthesized poly(propylene imine) dendrimers that are now produced at commercially relevant quantities (at multiple kilogram scale) worldwide. His dendrimers form the basic compound of a [[phosphate]] binder currently used in the clinic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.astellas.com/en/corporate/news/detail/astellas-receives-approval-for-2.html|title=2016 News Releases {{!}} Astellas Pharma Inc.|website=www.astellas.com|language=en|access-date=2017-07-19|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110224918/https://www.astellas.com/en/corporate/news/detail/astellas-receives-approval-for-2.html|archive-date=2017-11-10|url-status=dead}}</ref> Meijer also developed novel [[Organic electronics|semiconducting polymers]] with high electron mobilities.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sirringhaus|first1=H.|last2=Brown|first2=P. Meijer's discovery of ureidopyrimidinone-based supramolecular polymers<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cao|first1=Ke|last2=Liu|first2=Guoliang|date=2017-03-14|title=Low-Molecular-Weight, High-Mechanical-Strength, and Solution-Processable Telechelic Poly(ether imide) End-Capped with Ureidopyrimidinone|journal=Macromolecules|volume=50|issue=5|pages=2016–2023|doi=10.1021/acs.macromol.7b00156|bibcode=2017MaMol..50.2016C|issn=0024-9297}}</ref> is a landmark in supramolecular chemistry. He designed a simple quadruple [[Hydrogen bond|hydrogen-bonded]] building block that is self-complementary and exhibits a very large [[Binding constant|association constant]]. Bringing two of these units together with a [[Molecular spacer|spacer]] resulted in a supramolecular polymer with unprecedented properties. Depending on the conditions applied it on the one hand it possess all the properties of macromolecules, both in solution and solid state, while on the other hand it displays the dynamic nature of organic molecules tied together via [[Non-covalent interactions|non-covalent bonds]]. Today, the concept of supramolecular polymers is investigated in many international academic and industrial laboratories.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Markvoort|first1=Albert J.|last2=Eikelder|first2=Huub M. M. ten|last3=Hilbers|first3=Peter A. J.|last4=de Greef|first4=Tom F. A.|date=2016-04-27|title=Fragmentation and Coagulation in Supramolecular (Co)polymerization Kinetics|journal=ACS Central Science|volume=2|issue=4|pages=232–241|doi=10.1021/acscentsci.6b00009|doi-access=free|issn=2374-7943|pmc=4850513|pmid=27163054}}</ref> The Meijer lab has successfully started the company SupraPolix,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.suprapolix.com/|title=Welcome - SupraPolix|website=www.suprapolix.com|access-date=2017-07-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190909171814/http://www.suprapolix.com/|archive-date=2019-09-09|url-status=dead}}</ref> offering a supramolecular polymer platform as a key component in several applications, including glue (as superflow [[elastomer]]s), cosmetics and regenerative medicine of heart valves, for which [[clinical trial]]s are underway by the Dutch/Swiss company Xeltis.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.xeltis.com/news/xeltis-completes-patient-enrollment-xplore-trial/|title=Xeltis completes patient enrollment in Xplore-I trial {{!}} Xeltis|work=Xeltis|access-date=2017-07-20|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190209003351/http://xeltis.com/news/xeltis-completes-patient-enrollment-xplore-trial/|archive-date=2019-02-09|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Following up on his discovery Meijer has unraveled the mechanisms behind chemical [[self-assembly]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Berrocal|first1=José Augusto|last2=Zha|first2=R. Helen|last3=de Waal|first3=Bas F. M.|last4=Lugger|first4=Jody A. M.|last5=Lutz|first5=Martin|last6=Meijer|first6=E. W.|date=2017-04-25|title=Unraveling the Driving Forces in the Self-Assembly of Monodisperse Naphthalenediimide-Oligodimethylsiloxane Block Molecules|journal=ACS Nano|volume=11|issue=4|pages=3733–3741|doi=10.1021/acsnano.6b08380|issn=1936-0851|pmc=5406784|pmid=28380290}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Jabbari-Farouji|first1=S.|last2=van der Schoot|first2=Paul|date=2012-08-13|title=Theory of supramolecular co-polymerization in a two-component system|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=137|issue=6|pages=064906|doi=10.1063/1.4742192|pmid=22897310|issn=0021-9606|arxiv=1111.1767|bibcode=2012JChPh.137f4906J|s2cid=119310901}}</ref> and has proven that supramolecular polymerizations can be classified, based on their mechanism, in a way similar to conventional [[polymerization]]s.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Principles of Polymerization, Fourth Edition - Odian - Wiley Online Library|last=Odian|first=George|language=en|doi=10.1002/047147875x|year = 2004|isbn = 978-0471274001}}</ref> Current research in the Meijer lab focuses on complex multi-component supramolecular polymer systems and their assembly behaviour<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Haedler|first1=Andreas T.|last2=Meskers|first2=Stefan C. == Achievements and awards ==
[[File:Portrait Bert Meijer.jpg|alt=Portrait of Bert Meijer (2014)|left|frameless|Bert Meijer (2014)|border]]

=== Scientific output and research management ===
Meijer has published over 600 peer reviewed research articles and reviews which have been cited more than 100.000 times, yielding him an H-index of well over 142 [https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=0DiKroEAAAAJ&hl=en] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130606105728/http://scholar.google.com/citations?user=0DiKroEAAAAJ&hl=en |date=2013-06-06 }}. He guided 100+ PhD students and more than 25 of his former group members now hold tenured academic professorships worldwide. Meijer has over 20 patents and co-founded the companies SyMO-Chem,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.symo-chem.nl/|title=SyMO-Chem BV|website=www.symo-chem.nl|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190901000940/http://www.symo-chem.nl/|archive-date=2019-09-01|url-status=dead}}</ref> a professional contract research company (2000) and SupraPolix,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.suprapolix.com/|title=Welcome - SupraPolix|website=www.suprapolix.com|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190909171814/http://www.suprapolix.com/|archive-date=2019-09-09|url-status=dead}}</ref> focusing on supramolecular polymers (2003).

Since 2006 Meijer is the chairman of the International Scientific Advisory Board of DSM,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dsm.com/content/prcc/cworld/en_US/informationcenter-news/2007/06/26-07-scientific-advisory-board.html|title=DSM installs international Scientific Advisory Board|website=www.dsm.com|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728210238/https://www.dsm.com/content/prcc/cworld/en_US/informationcenter-news/2007/06/26-07-scientific-advisory-board.html|archive-date=2017-07-28|url-status=dead}}</ref> in 2008 he founded the Institute for Complex Molecular Systems<ref name=":0" /> at Eindhoven University of Technology, and he chairs the 27 million euro national Dutch research program into 'Functional Molecular Systems'<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fmsresearch.nl/|title=FMS Research Center – Research Center for Functional Molecular Systems|website=fmsresearch.nl|language=en-US|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190901031045/https://fmsresearch.nl/|archive-date=2019-09-01|url-status=dead}}</ref> since 2012. Between 2017 and 2023 Meijer was a member of the Board of Trustees of [[Leiden University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/news/2017/01/bert-meijer-joins-board-of-governors|title=Bert Meijer joins Board of Governors|website=Leiden University|date=31 January 2017 |language=en-US|access-date=2017-07-21}}</ref> Meijer also served as member of advisory or editorial boards of over 10 scientific journals, including [[Advanced Materials]] (since 1992), [[Angewandte Chemie]] (since 1998), [[Chemical Science (journal)|Chemical Science]] (since 2010) and the [[Journal of the American Chemical Society]] (since 2010).

=== Academic invitations and memberships ===
Meijer has obtained visiting professorships and was invited to named lectureships at many universities. He was visiting professor at the universities of Leuven, Belgium (1995), Illinois (1998), Bordeaux (2007), Zhejiang (2008) and California, Santa Barbara (2008). He currently is a Humboldt visiting professor at the Free University Berlin (until 2024). He has been, amongst others, Bayer distinguished lecturer (Cornell, New York, 1998), Glaxo-Wellcome lecturer (Sheffield, 1998), Rohm & Haas lecturer (Berkeley, 2002), Xerox Distinguished Lecturer of Canada (Toronto and Montreal, 2004), Melville Lecturer (Cambridge University, 2006) Mordecai and Rivka Rubin Lecturer (Technion, Israel, 2015), Aldrich Lecturer (Stanford University, USA, 2015) and Eastman Lecturer (North Carolina, 2016). He gave the Van ‘t Hoff Centennial lecture<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/awards/funding/van-t-hoff-fund/van-t-hoff-award-lectures|title=Van 't Hoff Award Lectures — KNAW|website=www.knaw.nl|language=en|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-date=2017-10-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171031042802/https://www.knaw.nl/en/awards/funding/van-t-hoff-fund/van-t-hoff-award-lectures|url-status=dead}}</ref> at the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences in 2001, the Carothers Lecture at Dupont Wilmington in 2005 and provided the keynote science lecture at Lowlands University 2009,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tue.nl/en/research/research-institutes/top-research-groups/institute-for-complex-molecular-systems/news-icms/14-09-2009-bert-meijer-at-lowlands-2009/|title=Bert Meijer at Lowlands 2009|website=www.tue.nl|language=en-US|access-date=2017-07-21}}{{Dead link|date=June 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> as part of the [[Lowlands (festival)|Lowlands music- and culture festival]] (Flevopolder, The Netherlands). In 2019, he was the Saul Winstein Lecturer at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chemistry.ucla.edu/news/2019-saul-winstein-lecture|title=Winstein lecture 2019|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200224152823/https://www.chemistry.ucla.edu/news/2019-saul-winstein-lecture |archive-date=2020-02-24 |access-date=}}</ref> and he was the 2020 Robert Robinson lecturer at the [[University of Oxford]]. He is also the 2025 Allan Hay lecturer at McGill University in Montreal.<ref>https://www.mcgill.ca/mc2/channels/event/chemical-society-seminar-allan-hay-lecture-bert-meijer-supramolecular-polymers-functional-materials-360987{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

Meijer is an elected member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (KNAW, since 2003)<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/5917 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200224144914/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/5917 |title=Bert Meijer |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=24 February 2020}}</ref> and the [[Koninklijke Hollandsche Maatschappij der Wetenschappen|Royal Holland Society of Sciences and Humanities]] (KHMW, since 1997), the [[Acatech|Deutsche Akademie der Technikwissenschaften]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.acatech.de/de/aktuelles-presse/presseinformationen-news/news-detail/artikel/verstaerkung-fuer-acatech-dreizehn-neue-mitglieder-in-die-deutsche-akademie-der-technikwissenschaft.html|title=News Detail|last=acatech|website=acatech - Die Deutsche Akademie der Technikwissenschaften|language=en|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171027175633/http://www.acatech.de/de/aktuelles-presse/presseinformationen-news/news-detail/artikel/verstaerkung-fuer-acatech-dreizehn-neue-mitglieder-in-die-deutsche-akademie-der-technikwissenschaft.html|archive-date=2017-10-27|url-status=dead}}</ref> since 2012), the Nordrhein-Westfälische Akademie der Wissenschaften und der Künste<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.awk.nrw.de/pressemedien/detailansicht-presse/2014-05-21-nordrhein-westfaelische-akademie-der-wissenschaften-und-der-kuenste-nimmt-17-neue-mitglieder-auf.html?tx_ttnews%5BbackPid%5D=51&cHash=a4e030ff372038360bbc7a690fb669e3|title=AWK: Detailansicht Presse|website=www.awk.nrw.de|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-date=2017-11-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110225340/http://www.awk.nrw.de/pressemedien/detailansicht-presse/2014-05-21-nordrhein-westfaelische-akademie-der-wissenschaften-und-der-kuenste-nimmt-17-neue-mitglieder-auf.html?tx_ttnews%5BbackPid%5D=51&cHash=a4e030ff372038360bbc7a690fb669e3|url-status=dead}}</ref> (since 2014), and the [[Academia Europaea]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Meijer_Egbert_Willem|title=Academy of Europe: Meijer Egbert Willem|last=Hoffmann|first=Ilire Hasani, Robert|website=www.ae-info.org|access-date=2017-07-21}}</ref> (since 2012). He is Honorary Fellow of the [[Chemical Research Society of India]] (since 2012) and Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/2015-aaas-fellows-recognized-contributions-advancing-science|title=2015 AAAS Fellows Recognized for Contributions to Advancing Science|date=2015-11-16|work=AAAS - The World's Largest General Scientific Society|access-date=2017-07-21|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190417215004/https://www.aaas.org/news/2015-aaas-fellows-recognized-contributions-advancing-science|archive-date=2019-04-17|url-status=dead}}</ref> (since 2015). Meijer is furthermore elected as an Honorary Member of the [[Royal Netherlands Chemical Society]] (KNCV, since 2018).<ref>[https://en.kncv.nl/kncv/honorary-members Honorary members] - website of the [[Royal Netherlands Chemical Society]]</ref> In 2019, he was elected as a member of the [[European Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurasc.org/user/677/egbert-meijer|title=European Academy of Sciences - Egbert Meijer|website=www.eurasc.org|access-date=2020-02-24}}</ref> and as International Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/bert-w-meijer|title=Bert W. Meijer|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en|access-date=2020-03-01}}</ref>

=== Awards ===
Meijer has received numerous prominent awards, including the Gold Medal of the [[Royal Netherlands Chemical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.kncv.nl/prijzen/kncv-gouden-medaille/winnaars-kncv-gouden-medaille|title=Winnaars KNCV Gouden Medaille - KNCV|website=www.kncv.nl|language=nl|access-date=2017-07-21}}</ref> (1993), the [[Spinoza Prize|Spinoza Award]] of the [[Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+in+alphabetical+order/bert+meijer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171031042807/https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+in+alphabetical+order/bert+meijer|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 31, 2017|title=Prof. E.W. (Bert) Meijer|last=|first=|date=|website=www.nwo.nl|language=en|access-date=2017-07-21}}</ref> (2001), the [[American Chemical Society|ACS]] Award in Polymer Chemistry<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/84/i3/ACS-Award-Polymer-Chemistry.html?type=paidArticleContent|title=ACS Award in Polymer Chemistry {{!}} Chemical & Engineering News|website=cen.acs.org|access-date=2017-07-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/acs-award-in-polymer-chemistry.html|title=ACS Award in Polymer Chemistry - American Chemical Society|website=American Chemical Society|language=en|access-date=2017-07-21}}</ref> (2006) and the [[AkzoNobel]] Science Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.akzonobel.com/for-media/media-releases-and-features/brilliant-scientist-wins-2010-akzonobel-science-award|title="Brilliant scientist" wins 2010 AkzoNobel Science Award {{!}} AkzoNobel|website=www.akzonobel.com|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171126203240/https://www.akzonobel.com/for-media/media-releases-and-features/brilliant-scientist-wins-2010-akzonobel-science-award|archive-date=2017-11-26|url-status=dead}}</ref> (2010). In 2010 he received an [[European Research Council|ERC]] Advanced Research Grant<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2010 |title=ERC Advanced Grants 2009 - Updated results (May 2010) - PHYSICAL SCIENCES AND ENGINEERING - List of projects invited for funding (alphabetical order) |url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/press_release/files/list_adg09_pe.pdf |access-date=2023-04-19 |website=erc.europa.eu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cordis.europa.eu/project/rcn/93962_en.html|title=European Commission : CORDIS : Projects & Results Service : From Supramolecular Polymers to Compartmentalized Systems|website=cordis.europa.eu|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181118035326/https://cordis.europa.eu/project/rcn/93962_en.html|archive-date=2018-11-18|url-status=dead}}</ref> and he was awarded the Wheland Medal of the [[University of Chicago]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.uchicago.edu/wheland-lecture|title=Wheland Lecture {{!}} University of Chicago Department of Chemistry|website=chemistry.uchicago.edu|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191001061908/https://chemistry.uchicago.edu/wheland-lecture|archive-date=2019-10-01|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the International Award of the [[Society of Polymer Science]] of Japan. In 2012 the ACS presented him the Arthur C. Cope Scholar Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/arthur-cope-scholar-award.html|title=Arthur C. Cope Scholar Awards - American Chemical Society|website=American Chemical Society|language=en|access-date=2017-07-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/90/i9/Arthur-C-Cope-Scholar-E.html?type=paidArticleContent|title=Arthur C. Cope Scholar E. W. (Bert) Meijer {{!}} Chemical & Engineering News|last=Halford|first=Bethany|website=cen.acs.org|access-date=2017-07-21}}</ref> In 2013 Meijer held the [[Solvay S.A.|Solvay]] International Chair in Chemistry,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.solvayinstitutes.be/html/chair.html|title=Solvay Institutes|website=www.solvayinstitutes.be|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-date=2023-12-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209161025/http://solvayinstitutes.be/html/chair.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> and in 2014 he won the Belgium Polymer Group Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.belgianpolymergroup.be/awards|title=awards {{!}} Belgian Polymer Group|website=www.belgianpolymergroup.be|language=en|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180919090557/http://www.belgianpolymergroup.be/awards|archive-date=2018-09-19|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the Prelog Medal of [[ETH Zurich|ETH Zürich]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chab.ethz.ch/en/research/institutes/LOC/prelog-lecture/past-prelog-lecturers-and-their-laudations.html|title=Past Prelog-Lecturers and Their Laudations|website=www.chab.ethz.ch|language=en|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-date=2017-10-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171026140947/https://www.chab.ethz.ch/en/research/institutes/LOC/prelog-lecture/past-prelog-lecturers-and-their-laudations.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> That same year he received the Academy Professor Prize<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/news/news/academy-professor-prize-awarded-to-dorret-boomsma-and-bert-meijer|title=Academy Professor Prize awarded to Dorret Boomsma and Bert Meijer — KNAW|website=www.knaw.nl|language=en|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-date=2014-05-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517151644/https://www.knaw.nl/en/news/news/academy-professor-prize-awarded-to-dorret-boomsma-and-bert-meijer|url-status=dead}}</ref> of the Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences appointed as a lifetime achievement award. In 2017 Meijer was installed Doctorem Honoris Causa at the [[University of Mons]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://portail.umons.ac.be/FR/actualites/Pages/DHCfacultaires2017.aspx|title=Université de Mons|website=portail.umons.ac.be|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111041629/https://portail.umons.ac.be/FR/actualites/Pages/DHCfacultaires2017.aspx|archive-date=2017-11-11|url-status=dead}}</ref> (Belgium) and awarded the Forschungspreis of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Humboldt Foundation]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/pls/web/pub_auswahlergebnisse.main|title=Alexander von Humboldt-Foundation - Auswahlergebnisse|website=www.humboldt-foundation.de|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-date=2019-08-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190820035258/http://www.humboldt-foundation.de/pls/web/pub_auswahlergebnisse.main|url-status=dead}}</ref> (Germany) and the Nagoya Gold Medal Award in Organic Chemistry<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fmsresearch.nl/2017/03/bert-meijer-awarded-prestigious-nagoya-gold-medal/|title=Bert Meijer awarded prestigious Nagoya Gold Medal – FMS Research Center|website=fmsresearch.nl|language=en-US|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181117233504/https://fmsresearch.nl/2017/03/bert-meijer-awarded-prestigious-nagoya-gold-medal/|archive-date=2018-11-17|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.msd-life-science-foundation.or.jp/en/symp/nagoya/nagoya_prog2017.html|title=The 23rd Nagoya Medal {{!}} MSD Life Science Foundation|website=www.msd-life-science-foundation.or.jp|language=ja|access-date=2017-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111041718/http://www.msd-life-science-foundation.or.jp/en/symp/nagoya/nagoya_prog2017.html|archive-date=2017-11-11|url-status=dead}}</ref> (Japan). In 2018, he was awarded a second ERC Advanced Research Grant<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/news/news/erc-advanced-grants-for-academy-members-and-young-academy-alumnus-april-2018|title=ERC Advanced Grants for Academy members and Young Academy alumnus — KNAW|website=www.knaw.nl|access-date=2020-02-24|archive-date=2020-02-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200224144904/https://www.knaw.nl/en/news/news/erc-advanced-grants-for-academy-members-and-young-academy-alumnus-april-2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the [[Chirality Medal]] of the [[Società Chimica Italiana]] (Princeton, 2018).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/1520636x/chiralityaward/page.html|title=Chirality|website=Wiley Online Library|doi=10.1002/(ISSN)1520-636X |language=en|access-date=2020-02-24}}</ref> In 2019, Bert Meijer was installed Doctorem Honoris Causa at the [[Free University of Berlin|Free University Berlin]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fu-berlin.de/presse/informationen/fup/2019/fup_19_229-ehrendoktorwuerde-bert-meijers/index.html|title=Freie Universität Berlin verleiht Ehrendoktorwürde für Prof. Dr. Egbert Willem Meijer|date=2019-07-29|website=www.fu-berlin.de|language=de|access-date=2020-02-24}}</ref> In 2020, he received the title of Commander of the [[Order of the Netherlands Lion]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tue.nl/en/news/news-overview/28-02-2020-bert-meijer-receives-the-title-of-commander-from-the-order-of-the-netherlands-lion/|title=Bert Meijer receives the title of Commander from the Order of the Netherlands Lion|website=www.tue.nl|language=English|access-date=2020-03-01}}</ref> the prestigious Dutch [[order of chivalry]] founded by [[William I of the Netherlands|King William I]] in 1815. On September 12, 2022, the [[German Chemical Society|German Chemical Society GDCh]] presented him the [[Hermann Staudinger Prize]] 2022<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hermann Staudinger Prize for Bert Meijer |url=https://www.tue.nl/en/news-and-events/news-overview/13-09-2022-hermann-staudinger-prize-for-bert-meijer/ |access-date=2022-09-15 |website=www.tue.nl |language=English}}</ref> for his 'outstanding and creative contributions to the field of supramolecular polymer chemistry'. In May 2024, the PTN Medema Lecture Award<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-05-23 |title=Medema Lecture Award {{!}} Polymer Technology Netherlands |url=https://ptn.nu/ptn-medema-lecture-award/ |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=ptn.nu |language=en-GB}}</ref> was received by Meijer for his excellence in polymer science and his strong connection with the Dutch polymer community. On February the 12th, 2025 Le Grand Prix de la Fondation de la [[Maison de la chimie|Maison de la Chimie]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Les lauréats de l'année |url=https://actions.maisondelachimie.com/les-prix-de-la-fondation/grand-prix-de-la-fondation/les-laureats-de-lannee/ |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=Fondation de la Maison de la Chimie |language=fr}}</ref> will be awarded to honor his work in supramolecular polymer chemistry, in particular via non non-covalent interactions that led him to the concept of "quadrupolar hydrogen bonds".

== Personal life ==
Meijer was born in 1955 as the oldest son of Roelof Meijer and Winy Meijer–de Wit (both civil servants). In 1979 he married Iektje Oosterbeek with whom he has two sons: Roger Meijer (1985) and Wieger Meijer (1988).
